rows.question: Can the Route10 power both of its PoE+ ports at the full 30 W per port at the same time?
rows.expected: No: 2 ports x 30 W = 60 W, but the Route10 PoE budget is 40 W
rows.answer: No, the Route10 cannot supply 30 W on both ports at once, because its total PoE budget is 40W. [1][2][4] Two ports at 30 W each would need 30 W + 30 W = 60 W, which exceeds the 40W budget by 20 W. [2][4] Each of the two ports is 802.3at PoE+ (54VDC, 0.6A max), so the 40W total is the limiting factor when both are in use. [1][4]

rows.question: Both fall detection papers use an ESP32. How does each one send its sensor data?

rows.question: What sampling rate does each fall detection paper use for its sensor data?
rows.expected: Adebesin et al.: 20 Hz (50 ms); bathroom study: streams mapped to a common 100 Hz
rows.answer: Adebesin et al. (2026) use a 20 Hz sampling rate (50 ms period): the wearable's ESP32 samples its sensors at 20 Hz, and Table 3 lists 20 Hz (50 ms) for both the IMU and piezoelectric configurations. [1][2][3] In that paper, lower-frequency baseline streams were linearly resampled to a uniform 20 Hz before windowing. [1] The bathroom fall detection paper (arXiv 2603.17069) has its mmWave radar node produce 3D point clouds at 12.5 Hz. [4] In the same paper, the triaxial vibration node sampled at 200 Hz and was resampled to 100 Hz. [5] Its preprocessing maps the raw radar and vibration streams to a common rate of fs = 100 Hz. [6]

rows.question: On the Raspberry Pi 4B, how does the end-to-end latency of the radar-only model compare with the radar and vibration fusion model in the bathroom study?
rows.expected: Radar only 28.4 ms vs fusion 15.8 ms
rows.answer: On the Raspberry Pi 4B, the radar-only Motion-Mamba model has an end-to-end latency of 28.4 ms (7.5 ms preprocessing, 19.8 ms inference). [1] The radar and vibration fusion model has an end-to-end latency of 15.8 ms (8.9 ms preprocessing, 6.7 ms inference). [2] The fusion model is therefore faster end-to-end by 28.4 ms - 15.8 ms = 12.6 ms, even though its preprocessing is slower (8.9 ms vs 7.5 ms) and its inference is faster (6.7 ms vs 19.8 ms). [1][2]

rows.answer:
The paper reports 10750 mJ per 2.56 s window for the proposed model, measured on the Raspberry Pi 4B gateway, not for the sensing nodes.
